speaker: Head Coach
quote_text:
Start with Dan. Evening, Michael. Just wonder  how satisfying does that feel, maybe seeing  
two different sides of your team this evening?  Yeah, we had to see a few sides actually tonight,  
and credit to Keith and his staff and the team,  because they're a good team. They're tough to play  
against. You know, they ask certain questions.  I thought we started fantastically in the game,  
looked really dangerous, probably could have had  an extra goal or two, and then they came into it  
a little bit. So half-time was a good position  for us to be in. We tweaked a couple of things  
at half-time and probably had a little bit more  control. The game wasn't as open, which at that  
stage is exactly what we kind of wanted really,  and seeing the game out in tough circumstances.  
So it's a big three points. You know, it's that  time of the season where results are crucial,  
you know, and the boys, to win again is a good  habit to get used to, but it's an important one  
for us. Casemiro with another big goal for  the team. Just wonder how much do you think  
he's enjoying these final games, especially at  Old Trafford, you know, this United club? Yeah,  
I think it's pretty clear how much it means to  him, you know, and probably the situation and  
the clarity of it has helped everything to be so  open and understood for the supporters as well,  
for him, for everybody. And it means a lot to him,  you know, and credit to him because the situation  
that it is, he's given absolutely everything as  well and had some big moments for us. So all round  
it's quite a nice kind of direction for it to be  taken. The formation changed in the second half.  
Roughly what time in the first half did you decide  that you were going to do that? Five minutes  
before half-time, maybe five, six minutes before  the second goal. Yeah, we just felt we were a  
little bit too open at certain times, and we still  could be dangerous, but we wanted to stop certain  
spaces and have a little bit more control within  the game and still carry the threat. So it was  
purely tactical. I think second half, we came out  and actually had control and still went forward,  
looked dangerous, and it was what the game needed  at that point really. So obviously the second  
goal, we were certain anyway, but the second goal  puts us in a great position then to have more  
control of the game. And yeah, in the end it's  gone to plan to a point and we've won the game,  
so we're happy with that. Just wanted to check,  so Diogo Dalot coming off was tactical? Tactical.  
Purely tactical, yeah. Pete. Hi, Michael. Another  impressive Kobbie display tonight. Was perhaps  
the most pleasing part of tonight his defensive  effort, flying into tackles, and is it something  
you've been working on behind the scenes? I just  thought on the back of the Chelsea game really,  
he's particularly good, and in the Chelsea game,  similar things. I think showing a little bit of  
everything what he can do. I think his build-up  play, his taking the ball, his creation, his  
starting the attacks, you know, he's so effective  with that. But definitely duels, one v ones,  
recovery, run back tackling. I think over the  last two games he's taken that up a level. So it's  
great to see that he can do it. We know he can do  it and try to give him more responsibility as the  
games go on. And still, listen, still not expect  too much of him as well and understand and try  
to help him a little bit. But he's doing great at  the moment. Just in terms of the Champions League,  
you must feel like you're pretty much there now.  I know it's not mathematical, but it's pretty  
much that. We've given ourselves a great chance,  you know. We've put ourselves in a big position.  
I think these last two results have been big to  that. It's a tough league, you know, it's tough to  
get wins. I think you can see that throughout the  league. So to get the amount of wins we've had,  
and especially after the setbacks, you know, the  Newcastle defeat, to then bounce back with Villa,  
the Leeds one, to bounce back again, I  think the lads have got to take a bit of  
credit for that because this week's been very  effective in terms of the league. You know, so  
the other side of it is Champions League is one  thing, but it's not something that we should be  
over celebrating either. You know, we want to be  finishing higher up the league really, and we want  
to be challenging higher up the league and trying  to get more points. So our season doesn't get to  
a close when that happens. I think it's one thing  certainly we need to try and achieve it, and we've  
put ourselves in a good position at this moment,  but there's still more work to be done. What more  
can you say about Bruno Fernandes? Another assist  tonight. He leads in all aspects of the game.  
You might not want to over celebrate Champions  League, but it feels like he should be celebrating  
some kind of end of season accolades. Yeah,  listen, hopefully he does. He deserves it,  
you know, for the impact that he's had and the  moments that he's created. I think whether that's  
creating, whether that's scoring, whether that's  having other influence within the group, you know,  
he's had a big season. You know, there's no  getting away from it and it was another good  
performance from him tonight. Tian. Hi, Michael.  It's bound to get asked every week if he keeps  
playing like that between now and the end of  the season, but as far as you're concerned,  
is Casemiro's situation this summer, is that  closed? Yeah, it's pretty clear, yeah. There's  
no way back kind of thing? No, but from both sides  it's pretty clear. Harry's just been on TV talking  
about being able to play two different systems.  Prior to you arriving back there were loads. Is  
that a massive strength, do you think, that you  can just switch it in game? They look a lot more  
comfortable now being able to do that. Yeah, I  think we've got to be able to adapt, you know, and  
play certain things. I'm not really a big numbers  formation kind of guy. I think it's certain games,  
certain things. I think you can put a formation or  numbers on paper, but actually the way you play,  
there's only certain moments that you're in them  numbers really, in possession, out of possession,  
whether you're pressing, whether you're a little  bit deeper. So the number side of it, it's not so  
much. It's what we're trying to achieve with it,  you know, and try and be flexible. And I thought  
Noussair came in again and did fantastically  well and played two positions. Just shows on  
the back of last week, he was very unlucky not to  be playing tonight, but he stepped in great. And  
flexibility is important, adapting is important,  and actually managing the game and what we need.  
And I thought we did that tonight. Carl and then  last question could start. Evening, Mr Carrick.  
Congratulations on the win. Stretford End is  chanting one more year for Casemiro. You said  
the situation was clear. Now he's got four games  left. How do you go about maximising his presence  
on the field, in the dressing room, everywhere? It  looks like in places Mainoo and others are trying  
to take some pages out of Cas's book as well. Cas  has had an influence within the group. You know,  
he's got huge experience. He's a big player. He's  achieved an awful lot in the game, and I have  
to say, since I've been, he's given everything  that he could possibly give. You know, even the  
situation's probably helped that, knowing exactly  where it's at. There's nothing to hide and he's  
thrown himself right into it. And it's football,  you know, it's football. Some players come and go.  
Players have come and left this football club over  the years, and you've got to evolve and you've got  
to move on and you've got to adapt, and that's  kind of the world we're in. But he's definitely  
given everything, and I think it's nice that  he's got that connection with the supporters  
and it comes from both ways, because I know he's  an emotional guy and it means a lot to him. Hi,  
Michael. Benjamin Šeško first half today, didn't  really get any chances until he scored the goal.  
He wasn't getting a lot. When you're on the back  foot and then he gets one chance and takes it,  
how important is that to have from a number  nine? It feels like since you've come in, that's  
something he's shown a lot, that he doesn't need  kind of getting warmed up with chances. He gets  
a chance, he takes it. Yeah, that's great. It's  great if he can score on the first one. I think  
I just think the way the game is at times now,  I think if you are an out and out number nine,  
the game kind of went away from it a little bit in  many ways, and it's kind of a bit untouchable. I  
think if you are an out and out striker that lives  on the last line and plays for those, I think  
sometimes you're not necessarily always involved  in the game, but that's not the role, you know.  
He's certainly got a part to play in link play  and out of possession and a role with that. But  
I think if you look at out and out number nines,  they're there to pick the moments and be there at  
the right time. And it was a big moment for us.  I thought he took this fantastically well. He was  
so calm and composed with it, and it just shows  the steps that he's made, I think, to be in that  
situation and have that confidence to put the  ball away like he did. All right, guys. Cheers.
title: Michael Carrick post-match press conference | Manchester United 2-1 Brentford | Premier League
